stem:
Which of the following is the most likely order of diagnoses for the five children described, matching the cases A–E?

A. 8-month-old boy, screaming and irritable with intermittent pallor, passed PR blood described as “blackcurrant jelly”.

B. 13-year-old girl with abdominal pain for three months.

C. 7-year-old girl with 24 hours of vomiting and anorexia, now pyrexial and pale, with right lower quadrant pain that started periumbilically.

D. 14-year-old boy with acute severe abdominal pain for 2 hours, cannot barely walk, no vomiting.

E. 6-week-old male infant with projectile non-bilious vomiting after feeds for two weeks, with wrinkled skin.
explanation: The correct sequence is B - E - C - A - D, which corresponds to the most likely diagnoses in the order given by the clinical features: chronic abdominal pain, pyloric stenosis, appendicitis, intussusception, and testicular torsion/acute scrotum-type presentation.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Abdominal pain

rationale: This is a matching-style item best preserved by selecting the existing option that contains the correct sequence.

optionExplanations.C: Correct: B is chronic abdominal pain/functional pain, E is pyloric stenosis with projectile non-bilious vomiting, C is appendicitis, A is intussusception, and D is acute torsion/acute abdominal emergency presentation.

source.quizTitle: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Abdominal pain
source.questionTextHtml:
A - 8 month old boy who is screaming and irritable, with pallor on and off. His parents think he has abdominal pain. He passed a small amount of PR blood earlier. His mum thought it looked like blackcurrant jelly.

B - 13 year old girl who has had abdominal pain for three months.

C - 7 year old girl who has had a few vomits for the past 24 hours and anorexia. She is now pyrexial and pale. She complains about abdominal pain in the lower right quadrant. She says the pain was previously more around the umbilicus.

D - 14 year old boy with acute onset abdominal pain, 8/10 in severity for 2 hours, who can barely walk. He has had no vomiting.

E - 6 week old male infant with projectile non-bilious vomiting after feeds for the past two weeks. His mum noted his skin has become wrinkly.

B - E - C - A - D
